text:
Korean shares rebounded over 6 percent Tuesday, recovering from a two-day rout, as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang's return to lead Nvidia. The Korean won was trading higher against the U.S. dollar.
The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) added 297.49 points, or 6.32 percent, to end at 5,006.03 after reaching as high as 5,065.74.
As the rally gathered momentum, the Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar at 9:06 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes.
The measure is triggered when KOSPI 200 futures rise at least 5 percent and remain at that level for one minute or longer.
Overnight, technology stocks on Wall Street surged after Nvidia's board decided to reinstate Huang, triggering a relief rally in battered artificial intelligence (AI) stocks.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3.01 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite surged 6.51 percent.
